title: Tit for tat
src: Robert Axelrod, The Evolution of Cooperation, 1984
idea: In repeated games, a strategy that starts friendly, copies the other side's last move, and forgives quickly beat far more complicated rivals in Axelrod's tournaments.
apply: In an ongoing relationship, start with good faith, answer an unfair move once and clearly, then return to cooperation.
remind: Start kind. Answer once. Forgive fast.
who: Hugo, who deals with the same supplier every month.

items.x: Each side can be generous or sharp
They will deal again next month

scenes.nar: Hugo orders from the same supplier every month. Each side can be generous or sharp, and they will deal again next month.

items.x: Always give in: they take advantage
Always retaliate: every month is a fight

scenes.nar: Always giving in invites being taken advantage of. Always retaliating turns every month into a fight.
In Axelrod's tournaments, tit for tat won. Be nice first, respond to unfairness once, forgive quickly, and be predictable.

items.x: Late delivery: one calm, firm email

scenes.nar: When a delivery is late, Hugo sends one firm email. The supplier fixes it, the relationship resets, and better terms follow.
